name: German Fruit Pie
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: heaping teaspoonful of baking powder
ingredients.originalText: a heaping teaspoonful of baking powder

ingredients.name: piece of butter as large as a walnut
ingredients.originalText: a piece of butter as large as a walnut

instructions.text: Sift together a heaping teaspoonful of baking powder and a pint of flour
add a piece of butter as large as a walnut, a pinch of salt, one beaten egg and sweet milk enough to make a soft dough
Roll it out half an inch thick
butter a square biscuit tin and cover the bottom and sides with the dough
fill the pan with quartered juicy apples, sprinkle with a little cinnamon and molasses
Bake in rather quick oven until the crust and apples are cooked a light brown
Sprinkle a little sugar over the top five minutes before removing from the oven

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift together a heaping teaspoonful of baking powder and a pint of flour
2. add a piece of butter as large as a walnut, a pinch of salt, one beaten egg and sweet milk enough to make a soft dough
3. Roll it out half an inch thick
4. butter a square biscuit tin and cover the bottom and sides with the dough
5. fill the pan with quartered juicy apples, sprinkle with a little cinnamon and molasses
6. Bake in rather quick oven until the crust and apples are cooked a light brown
7. Sprinkle a little sugar over the top five minutes before removing from the oven
